Tax Plan | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Tax Plan From the moment I took office, my top priority has been standing up for New York taxpayers. Keeping America competitive and free means having a tax system that rewards hard work, fuels entrepreneurship, and lets families and businesses grow and succeed. I am the only New York Republican who voted for both of President Trump’s landmark tax bills: the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) in 2017 and H.R. 1, the Working Families Tax Cuts. Both laws delivered historic relief by lowering rates for individuals and businesses, doubling the Standard Deduction and the Child Tax Credit, and driving private investment and job growth across the country. As a member of the House Ways and Means Committee, responsible for overseeing federal tax policy, I played a pivotal role in crafting H.R. 1’s comprehensive tax relief. On July 4, 2025, President Trump signed H.R. 1 into law. This is a transformative, pro-growth, pro-worker, and pro-family tax package that locks in and expands the successes of TCJA. The Working Families Tax Cuts makes the 20% small business deduction permanent, raises the standard deduction, and restores full expensing for equipment purchases. It protects family farms from the estate tax, bolsters the Child Tax Credit, and allows independent contractors, truckers, and gig workers to focus on their businesses instead of getting bogged down with 1099 forms and IRS paperwork. H.R. 1 also makes the New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC), a long-standing priority of mine, a permanent fixture of the tax code. NMTC permanence establishes long-term certainty for private investors and community development organizations so that they can invest in communities across New York’s 24 th Congressional District. The credit offers a 39% federal tax credit for investments made in low-income, economically distressed areas, encouraging job creation, business development, and infrastructure growth.  Our focus should be on giving families and taxpayers more flexibility, more opportunity, and more control over their hard-earned money. Iran remains the greatest threat to peace in the Middle East as it relentlessly pursues a nuclear weapon and finances terrorism against Israel and the United States. Veterans Plan | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Veterans Plan America’s veterans risked their lives to defend our great nation and protect our freedoms. As the mother of a Marine officer, I understand the sacrifices that are made by our service members and their families every day. One of my top priorities in Congress is to ensure every American service member and veteran is well-equipped and adequately supported, whether they are actively serving our country or transitioning back to civilian life. Congress, the Department of War (DOW), and the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) have a duty to serve our military community. All programs dedicated to veterans must be transparent, effective, and affordable. Due to historical issues within the VA, such as misappropriation of funds, inconsistent delivery of quality healthcare, and claims backlogs, I will ensure the VA continues to undergo the reforms necessary to fulfill its mission of supporting our veterans. I am committed to supporting legislation that reaffirms our nation’s commitment to the men and women who served our nation and courageously fought for our freedoms. House Republicans have upheld their commitment to our nation’s veterans during the 119th Congress by passing legislation, including H.R. 1663, the Veterans Scam and Fraud Evasion Act of 2025. This bill, which I cosponsored and supported, reforms the VA by establishing stronger protections for veterans against fraud. Additionally, I voted to support H.R. 6047, the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act of 2025, which increases the supplemental monthly payment for certain severely disabled veterans receiving the highest levels of aid and attendance compensation, expands VA home loan eligibility to certain members of the National Guard and Reserve, and provides surviving spouses with greater benefit stability. Agriculture Plan | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Agriculture Plan Agriculture is the foundation of our regional economy. New York’s 24th Congressional District is the largest agricultural district in the Northeast and the 5th largest dairy-producing district in the United States. It includes Wayne County, the 3rd largest apple-producing county nationwide and the largest outside Washington State. Wyoming County is also among the nation’s leading maple syrup-producing counties, while the Finger Lakes is internationally recognized for its vineyards, orchards, and specialty crops. These producers drive our local economy, create jobs throughout the region, and provide our grocery stores and schools with nutritious, locally produced food. In recent years, however, farmers and agricultural producers have faced mounting pressure from unfair foreign trade practices and burdensome policies at both the state and federal levels. Agriculture is essential to the strength of our communities, supporting critical jobs and economic opportunities across the region. We must enact commonsense policies that allow our farmers and rural communities to remain competitive in the global marketplace. I support a comprehensive strategy that advances pro-farmer policies and strengthens the programs necessary to maintain a thriving domestic food supply. My plan will expand opportunities throughout our rural communities, protect American agriculture from hostile foreign interference, and provide farmers and producers with the stability and resources they need to succeed. Promoting a Strong and Reliable Farm Economy Voted for H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act : Finally, after a three-year delay, the House of Representatives has passed a full 5-year farm bill. While many key Farm Bill provisions were included in H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, there was still much work to be done. This farm bill strengthens protections for specialty crop emergency assistance, extends key dairy provisions, and enhances oversight of foreign ownership of American farmland. Law Enforcement Plan | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Law Enforcement Plan More than 800,000 law enforcement officers across the United States serve and protect our communities at great personal risk. These public servants intervene daily in dangerous situations to de-escalate tensions, provide emergency care, apprehend criminals, defend the most vulnerable, and protect the constitutional rights of all Americans. Over the past few years, law enforcement officers have faced unprecedented challenges, including a rising rate of violence against officers and the left’s efforts to undermine officers’ ability to do their jobs safely. From 2021 through 2025, 311 law enforcement officers were feloniously killed in the line of duty, with the 2021–2024 total marking the highest number for any consecutive four-year period in FBI data. Amid these unparalleled challenges, politicians in Washington and across the country have perpetuated the damaging idea that law enforcement officers are the enemy. They have even gone so far as to create a dangerous movement to defund and demoralize the police. Additionally, New York State’s fiscal year 2027 budget, signed by Governor Hochul, bans local law enforcement agencies from entering into or renewing 287(g) agreements with ICE. Cooperation among federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies is essential to keeping New Yorkers safe, which is why  I condemned this harmful action by Governor Hochul. These attacks on our law enforcement officers and the demonization of police imperil our public safety and needlessly divide communities. In response, I am supporting a multipronged plan to support law enforcement and bring our communities back together. We must move beyond divisive and damaging rhetoric, mend relationships between police and the communities they serve, and provide our police officers with the legal protections and tools they need to do their jobs safely and effectively. Border Security Plan | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Border Security Plan Under the leadership of President Donald Trump and NY-24 resident Border Czar Tom Homan, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and other federal agencies have taken immediate action to stop illegal immigration, drug and weapons trafficking, and criminal gang activity from entering our communities. Through this coordination, federal agencies have created a deterrent effect, reducing illegal entries to historic lows. Under former President Biden’s administration, over 10 million illegal aliens entered our country without vetting or background checks, creating the worst humanitarian crisis our nation has faced in more than two decades. Every year the Biden administration set new records for illegal border crossings. During the first year of President Trump’s second term, we secured our border, apprehended and deported thousands of criminal illegal aliens, and worked to safeguard our communities against dangerous fentanyl smuggling and human trafficking. Congress successfully passed H.R. 1, which allocated billions of dollars to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to hire more officers and complete the border wall. Unfortunately, Governor Kathy Hochul and Albany Democrats have sought to restrict cooperation between local law enforcement and federal immigration authorities. New York State’s Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 Enacted Budget, signed by Governor Hochul, prohibits local law enforcement agencies from entering into or renewing 287(g) agreements with ICE. Cooperation among federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies is essential to keeping New Yorkers safe, which is why  I condemned this harmful action  by Governor Hochul. Additionally,  I urged Governor Hochul to reverse the State’s decision  not to apply for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's State Border Security Reinforcement Fund (SBSRF), which provides reimbursement for expenses made by States to detect illicit drugs, combat human trafficking, apprehend illegal aliens, and strengthen public safety along the border. Second Amendment Plan | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Second Amendment Plan For more than 200 years, sportsmen, hunters, and lawful gun owners have embraced our Second Amendment rights, which we all share as Americans. When the Founding Fathers were writing the Bill of Rights, they specifically included the Second Amendment to ensure that every American had “the right… to keep and bear Arms.” They went on to affirm that this right “shall not be infringed.” One of my top priorities has been to preserve and uphold this sacred right for law-abiding citizens. In 2021, I led an amicus brief co-signed by 175 of my colleagues urging the Supreme Court to rule in NYSRPA v. Bruen that New York’s concealed carry law was unconstitutional. In 2022, the Supreme Court agreed with my arguments and struck down New York’s restrictive concealed carry law, and Justice Clarence Thomas even cited our brief in his decision. NYSRPA v. Bruen was the most significant Second Amendment win in over a decade, and it represents a major step in restoring our Founders’ vision for our Constitutional freedoms. During my time in the New York State Assembly, I opposed the onerous NY SAFE Act and was the first to introduce formal legislation to repeal this law that infringed on the rights of all law-abiding gun owners. In Congress, I have continued to fight against Congressional Democrats’ and the Hochul administration’s attempts to criminalize legal gun ownership and violate our Constitutional rights. As a Constitutional Conservative, I find it imperative that Americans continue to have the right to protect themselves under the Second Amendment. That is why I have cosponsored many bills, such as the National Constitutional Carry Act and the Protecting the Right to Keep and Bear Arms Act, to ensure American citizens’ Second Amendment right to carry is protected and not infringed. Additionally, I cosponsored and voted to pass H.R. 1181, the Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act, prohibiting payment card networks from creating a new Merchant Category Code (MCC) exclusively for firearm retailers, which would infringe on law-abiding citizens’ privacy rights. Make Voting Great Again | Representative Claudia Tenney Skip to main content Make Voting Great Again Free and fair elections are the cornerstone of our Constitutional Republic. Voting is a powerful expression of self-governance and the most sacred right we hold as Americans. Congress must focus on safeguarding the public's trust in our democratic process and promoting strong participation by qualified voters in every election. The United States was founded on the principles of democracy and self-determination, and election integrity forms the foundation that enables our representative system to work. Free and fair elections ensure that government authority derives from the consent of the governed, upholding the legitimacy and stability of our political system. Therefore, protecting elections from fraud, interference, and administrative mistakes is essential to preserving our democracy and ensuring that governance remains with the people.  In recent years, election integrity issues have rightly come to the forefront. Concerns such as voter fraud, cybersecurity threats, and burdensome administrative challenges have highlighted the need for strong measures to safeguard the electoral process. As a result, many Americans have lost confidence in the fairness of elections, undermining faith in our institutions.  Restoring faith in the electoral system requires comprehensive reforms that enhance security, transparency, and accountability. These reforms must ensure that eligible American citizens can exercise their right to vote freely while safeguarding against fraud and administrative errors.
